weave-lines.note: At 1280 and 390, on ink and paper, the field reads as cloth and not as a net: short horizontal and vertical ribbon bars alternate over and under along every row and column, each ribbon shows two edge hairlines, and the 6px gutters stay open (ribbon 0.75 of a 24px pitch). The under strand's edges visibly stop before the over strand, so no edge is drawn through a crossing, and the field is clearly not hatch-lines, grid-paper or brick-lattice. At 390 the same 24px pitch is cut cleanly at the frame with no stub. At strength 0.35 the lines are faint on ink and slightly firmer on paper, and the headline and copy stay readable on both. The tile period is 2 times float times pitch, as briefed, and the path keeps whole-pixel runs on half-pixel lines. Alternate props now checked from the geo captures at 1280 and 390 on ink and paper; the paper ground is a light grey with black copy, so it is truly paper. Float 2 breaks the surface into 2 by 2 blocks of horizontal and vertical ribbons, a basket weave, with four edge lines per block. Float 3 gives 3 by 3 blocks with six lines each. In both, the over block's edges run unbroken, and the under strands' edges stop a visible 3px short of the neighbouring block, so the over and under reading holds and the field never turns into a plain grid. The native 64px seam crops at the first interior seam show the lines continuing across the tile join with no gap, doubled line or step, and the full captures show no seam at any tile boundary. At 390 the blocks are cut at the frame without a stub. The heading and copy stay readable on both grounds, with only faint hairlines passing behind the glyphs. No material issue. Residual limit: the seam crops are 64px at 1x, so crispness is judged from clean single-pixel lines at native size and not from a magnified diff.

triangular-mesh.note: The revision landed. At 1280 on ink and paper there are four mint marks, inside the briefed three to five: about x 665 y 60, x 869 y 354, x 190 y 400 and x 486 y 599. They are spread across the top, the middle and the lower half, with none clustered and none under the heading or the copy line, which ends at x 465 and y 77, well clear of the nearest mark. The earlier cluster in the right middle is gone, and every mark is at least 40px from any frame edge. At 390 on both grounds a single mark sits at x 190 y 400, centred and clear of the text and the edges. The wireframe still reads distinctly: every face is a triangle of a different shape, no edges cross and no face looks flipped, there is a dot at each interior node, rows and columns stay legible under the jitter, and the mesh reaches all four sides at the same 48px spacing. The edges stay quiet under the heading on both grounds. The core now defaults marks to 1 and carries a 2px mark inset. The brief now says about three to five marks at the 1 percent default in a 1280 by 800 frame, and its prop line says default 1, so the code, the brief and the captures agree. Residual risk: the captures are 1x, so I cannot confirm the inset to the pixel; no mark comes near an edge in them. Marks are seed dependent, so a seed other than 1 may cluster or land on the copy, which is a user choice. Only default props were captured.

step-diagonals.note: At 1280 and 390 on both grounds the staircases are strictly horizontal and vertical, with equal 12px treads and risers at about 45 degrees, square corners, and channels four risers apart that are staircases themselves. No oblique stroke appears, so it is not diagonal-stripes, and the 390 frame is cut at the edge with no partial corner or stub. No gap or doubled corner shows where tiles meet at any captured size, and the lines look single-pixel and unblurred. The headline and copy stay readable at strength 0.3 on ink and paper; the paper capture is the firmer of the two. On the tile change: the builder was right and the brief was wrong. A staircase is invariant under a shift of one tread right and one riser up, not under a pure horizontal shift of one tread, so a tile run times step wide cannot repeat across without breaking the stair. The shipped tile is run times step times spacing wide by step times spacing tall, which is the smallest rectangle that repeats exactly, and the path is overdrawn a tread past each side so corners are whole. The source brief has since been corrected to describe that tile, so the brief and the build now agree. Run 3 with falling direction is now checked at 1280 and 390 on ink and paper (the paper ground is a light grey with black copy): treads of 36px and risers of 12px descend to the right as a shallower stair, every segment is horizontal or vertical, corners are square, lines are single pixel and unblurred, and the mirrored transform shows no blur or offset. The full captures show continuous staircases across every 144px tile boundary with no gap or doubled corner, and the 390 frame is cut cleanly at the edge. The copy stays readable on both grounds. No material issue. Residual limit: the 64px seam crops for this variant land on the heading text, so they add little, and the seam call rests on the full captures; the stroke stays at 1px at 1x only.
